material_scope_corrections.producer_claim: On 409, read result U and verify expected head SHA/method/action match the intended transaction before relying on it.
material_scope_corrections.correction: GitHub documents expected_head_sha, merge_method and merge_action in the result while the async request is still queued/pending. Once completed, the documented guarantee narrows to merged outcome/merge commit OID or failure reason; the public docs do not guarantee that the original intent tuple remains present in terminal result payloads. Therefore a 409 is safely reusable by GET-result intent comparison only when the returned result actually exposes those intent fields (or durable preexisting request metadata exists). If the request is already terminal and intent metadata is absent, preserve UNKNOWN about request identity and reconstruct only outcome from authoritative PR/queue/merge state.

unchanged_safe_conclusions: Final merge readiness is a policy-family proof problem rather than one CI boolean.
A green PR-head state is insufficient when merge-queue or other unevaluated policy families remain active.

Immutable payloads followed by one per-file CAS pointer remain a safer connected staged-publication pattern than sequentially rewriting several mutable files, but this is a recovery pattern rather than multi-file atomicity.
